name: Concept: sql-injection

name: Concept: sqli-blind-boolean

name: Concept: ssti

name: Concept: path-traversal

name: Concept: jwt-none-bypass
description: If the token says which algorithm to verify with, the token controls verification. Typical signals: alg field honoured from the header; verification library called without an allowlist.

name: Concept: jwt-alg-confusion
description: A public key is public; using it as a symmetric secret collapses the trust model. Typical signals: RS256 tokens plus a reachable public key; one verify call handling both key types.

name: Concept: auth-bypass
description: Authentication that can be satisfied by data the user controls is not authentication. Typical signals: role stored client-side; trust in a header set by the client; predictable session tokens.

name: Concept: idor
description: Knowing an identifier is not the same as being allowed to use it. Typical signals: sequential ids in URLs; object fetched before ownership is checked.

name: Concept: xss-reflected
description: Output encoding is context-dependent; HTML-escaping does not protect a JavaScript context. Typical signals: input echoed into the page; escaping applied for the wrong context.

name: Concept: ssrf
description: A server fetching a URL for you is a request that carries the server's trust, not yours. Typical signals: server-side fetch of a user URL; allowlist done on the string not the resolved address.

name: Concept: xxe
description: XML parsers that resolve external entities turn a document into a file-read primitive. Typical signals: XML upload or SOAP endpoint; parser configured with defaults.

name: Concept: deserialization-rce
description: Deserializing untrusted bytes can construct objects, and constructing objects runs code. Typical signals: serialized blobs in cookies or parameters; language-specific magic bytes.

name: Concept: race-condition
description: A check and the action it guards are two events; anything can happen in between. Typical signals: balance or quota checked then modified; no transaction or lock around the pair.

name: Concept: prototype-pollution
description: Recursive merges over untrusted keys can reach shared object internals. Typical signals: deep merge or clone helpers; config built from user JSON.

name: Concept: stack-buffer-overflow
description: Writing past a fixed buffer overwrites the stack state that tells the CPU where to return. Typical signals: unbounded copy functions; fixed-size local buffer; no bounds check on a length.

name: Concept: ret2libc
description: When you cannot run your own code, run code that is already there. Typical signals: NX enabled; dynamically linked; an address leak available.

name: Concept: rop-chain
description: Short instruction sequences ending in a return can be strung together into a program. Typical signals: NX and ASLR both on; no convenient single function to call.

name: Concept: format-string
description: A format string taken from input is an interpreter for reading and writing memory. Typical signals: user data passed as the format argument; unexpected output containing stack values.

name: Concept: canary-bypass
description: A canary only helps if the attacker cannot learn it or can avoid crossing it. Typical signals: stack protector present; a separate leak primitive; overwrite that skips the canary.

name: Concept: aslr-bypass
description: Randomised layout stops guessing, not leaking; one real address often reveals the rest. Typical signals: PIE enabled; some pointer printed or reflected; partial overwrite possible.

name: Concept: heap-overflow
description: Allocator metadata lives next to your data, so overflowing data corrupts bookkeeping. Typical signals: custom allocator or note-style menu; size and copy length come from different places.

name: Concept: use-after-free
description: Freeing memory without clearing the pointer leaves a handle to someone else's data. Typical signals: delete option that does not null the pointer; objects with function pointers.

name: Concept: integer-overflow
description: Arithmetic on sizes wraps, so a validated length can still produce a tiny allocation. Typical signals: size computed by multiplication or addition; signed/unsigned comparison.

name: Concept: off-by-one
description: A single byte past the end is enough when that byte is structurally important. Typical signals: loop bound using <= instead of <; length that forgets the terminator.

name: Concept: xor-single-byte
description: A one-byte key has 256 possibilities, so scoring plausible plaintext beats cleverness. Typical signals: uniform-looking bytes of modest length; repeating byte patterns matching spaces.

name: Concept: xor-repeating-key
description: Key reuse turns one hard problem into many easy single-byte problems. Typical signals: repeating structure at a fixed stride; ciphertext much longer than any plausible key.

name: Concept: rsa-small-e
description: Without padding, a small exponent on a small message never wraps the modulus. Typical signals: e equal to 3; no padding scheme mentioned; short plaintext.

name: Concept: rsa-common-modulus
description: Two coprime exponents over one modulus let you combine ciphertexts without the key. Typical signals: same n appears twice; two different public exponents.

name: Concept: rsa-factorisation
description: RSA's security rests entirely on factoring being hard for that particular modulus. Typical signals: small modulus; primes suspiciously close together; modulus appears in a public database.

name: Concept: padding-oracle
description: Any observable difference between 'bad padding' and 'bad content' leaks the plaintext. Typical signals: CBC mode; distinguishable error responses; decryption endpoint accepting ciphertext.

name: Concept: ecb-byte-at-a-time
description: ECB encrypts identical blocks identically, so alignment turns encryption into a lookup table. Typical signals: repeated ciphertext blocks; attacker-controlled prefix; no IV.

name: Concept: hash-length-extension
description: Merkle-Damgard hashes can be continued from a digest, so secret-prefix MACs are forgeable. Typical signals: MAC built as hash(secret + message); digest and message both visible.

name: Concept: classical-substitution
description: Substitution preserves letter frequency and word shape, which is exactly what breaks it. Typical signals: preserved word lengths and punctuation; letter distribution matching natural language.

name: Concept: classical-caesar
description: With only 25 shifts, exhaustive search is the correct first move. Typical signals: letter-only ciphertext; shifted but recognisable word shapes.

name: Concept: encoding-recognition
description: Identify the encoding from its alphabet and padding before trying to decode anything. Typical signals: restricted character set; length a multiple of four; trailing padding characters.

name: Concept: multilayer-encoding
description: Decoding is iterative; each layer tells you what the next one is. Typical signals: decoded output that is itself valid encoded text; gzip magic bytes after a decode.

name: Concept: string-decryption
description: Strings that are absent from the binary are usually built at runtime by a small routine. Typical signals: no useful output from strings; a loop over a data blob near startup.

name: Concept: algorithm-recovery
description: The goal is understanding the transformation well enough to invert it, not reading every instruction. Typical signals: a check function comparing against a constant; recognisable constants from known algorithms.

name: Concept: anti-debug-bypass
description: Anti-debugging checks are ordinary code paths and can be understood like any other branch. Typical signals: process tracing calls; timing comparisons; different behaviour under a debugger.

name: Concept: packed-binary
description: A packer replaces the real code with a stub that reconstructs it, so find the moment after unpacking. Typical signals: very few imports; high entropy sections; unusual section names.

name: Concept: vm-obfuscation
description: A bytecode interpreter moves the logic into data, so recover the instruction set first. Typical signals: a large dispatch switch; a byte array driving control flow; an instruction pointer variable.

name: Concept: control-flow-flattening
description: Flattening hides order, not logic; recovering the state transitions restores the original flow. Typical signals: a single loop with a large switch; a state variable assigned in every block.

name: Concept: pcap-carving
description: A capture is a transcript; follow the conversation rather than reading packets one by one. Typical signals: HTTP or FTP traffic in the capture; large transfers between two endpoints.

name: Concept: file-carving
description: Files are recognisable by their headers and footers even when the filesystem has forgotten them. Typical signals: a disk image or blob larger than its visible contents; magic bytes mid-file.

name: Concept: image-metadata
description: Photographs carry structured metadata that is easy to forget and easy to read. Typical signals: camera-generated image; unusually large metadata block.

name: Concept: steganography
description: Check structure before tooling; most 'stego' is data appended or stored in an extra chunk. Typical signals: file larger than its visible content; unexpected chunks; noise in the lowest bits.

name: Concept: memory-forensics
description: A memory image captures what was true at one instant, including things never written to disk. Typical signals: a memory dump; process list expectations; credential material in RAM.

name: Concept: log-analysis
description: Anomalies stand out against a baseline, so establish normal before hunting for strange. Typical signals: large log files; timestamps clustering unusually; rare user agents or status codes.

name: Concept: osint-geolocation
description: Narrow by what cannot change: architecture, signage, vegetation, sun angle. Typical signals: identifiable landmarks; language on signage; distinctive infrastructure.

name: Concept: osint-username
description: People reuse handles; correlation across platforms builds a picture no single site holds. Typical signals: a distinctive handle; cross-posted content; consistent avatars.

name: Concept: osint-domain-dns
description: Infrastructure has history, and history is frequently public. Typical signals: subdomains in certificate logs; historical DNS records; registration metadata.

name: Concept: nested-archive
description: Automate the repetitive part, but cap the depth so a zip bomb cannot exhaust the machine. Typical signals: archive containing exactly one archive; many repetitive extraction layers.

name: Concept: esoteric-lang
description: Identify the language from its character set, then use an interpreter rather than reading it. Typical signals: a tiny symbol alphabet; whitespace-only content; extremely repetitive text.

name: Concept: reentrancy
description: An external call hands control away; state must be settled before that happens. Typical signals: external call before a state update; no reentrancy guard; balance written after transfer.

name: Concept: access-control
description: A privileged function without an ownership check is a public function. Typical signals: sensitive function with no modifier; initialiser callable more than once.

name: Concept: integer-accounting
description: Rounding and unchecked arithmetic in accounting logic quietly redistribute value. Typical signals: unchecked arithmetic blocks; division before multiplication; share calculations.

name: Concept: android-exported-component
description: Anything exported in the manifest is reachable by any other app on the device. Typical signals: exported flag set true; intent filters on sensitive components; no permission attribute.

name: Concept: insecure-storage
description: On-device storage is readable given device access; encoding is not protection. Typical signals: credentials in preferences files; unencrypted local database; tokens in logs.

name: Concept: hardcoded-secret
description: A secret shipped to the client is a secret the client owns. Typical signals: API keys in resources; credentials in decompiled source; keys in native libraries.

name: Concept: certificate-pinning-bypass
description: Pinning is a client-side check, and client-side checks run on hardware the user controls. Typical signals: pinned certificates in the app; traffic invisible to a proxy.

name: Foundation: android-basics
description: APK layout, manifest, activities/services, and local storage. Needed before: android-exported-component, insecure-storage.

name: Foundation: aslr
description: Address Space Layout Randomization — addresses change per run. Needed before: aslr-bypass.

name: Foundation: assembly-basics
description: Registers, instructions, control flow in disassembly. Needed before: anti-debug-bypass, string-decryption.

name: Foundation: auth-bypass
description: Authentication checks that can be skipped or forged (claims, cookies, tokens). Needed before: jwt-alg-confusion, jwt-none-bypass.

name: Foundation: block-ciphers
description: Fixed-size block encryption (AES, DES) and modes of operation. Needed before: padding-oracle.

name: Foundation: c-memory
description: Stack vs heap, buffers, pointers, and undefined behavior in C. Needed before: format-string, stack-buffer-overflow.

name: Foundation: calling-convention
description: How arguments and return addresses are passed (x86/x64). Needed before: stack-buffer-overflow.

name: Foundation: canary
description: Stack canary/cookie checked before return to detect overflows. Needed before: canary-bypass.

name: Foundation: cbc
description: Cipher Block Chaining — chaining IV and previous ciphertext blocks. Needed before: padding-oracle.

name: Foundation: debugger-basics
description: Breakpoints, stepping, registers, and memory in a debugger. Needed before: anti-debug-bypass.

name: Foundation: encoding-basics
description: Base64, hex, URL encoding — reversible representations, not encryption. Needed before: xor-single-byte.

name: Foundation: file-carving
description: Recovering files from blobs by magic bytes and structure. Needed before: pcap-carving, steganography.

name: Foundation: file-formats
description: ELF/PE/Mach-O structure, sections, and headers. Needed before: packed-binary.

name: Foundation: frequency-analysis
description: Letter/byte frequency used to recover classical or XOR keys. Needed before: xor-repeating-key.

name: Foundation: gadgets
description: Short instruction sequences ending in ret, used to build ROP chains. Needed before: rop-chain.

name: Foundation: http-basics
description: HTTP methods, status codes, headers, cookies, and request/response structure. Needed before: sql-injection, ssrf, xss-reflected.

name: Foundation: image-formats
description: PNG/JPEG structure and common stego channels. Needed before: steganography.

name: Foundation: jwt-basics
description: JSON Web Tokens: header.payload.signature; alg selects the verification method. Needed before: jwt-alg-confusion, jwt-none-bypass.

name: Foundation: modular-arithmetic
description: Working modulo n; small e and related-message attacks. Needed before: rsa-small-e.

name: Foundation: network-basics
description: TCP/UDP, HTTP inside PCAP, streams and sessions. Needed before: pcap-carving.

name: Foundation: nx
description: Non-executable stack/heap — forces code reuse (ret2libc/ROP) instead of shellcode. Needed before: ret2libc, rop-chain.

name: Foundation: osint-basics
description: Public sources, correlation, and verification of open data. Needed before: osint-geolocation.

name: Foundation: plt-got
description: Procedure Linkage Table / Global Offset Table used for dynamic linking. Needed before: ret2libc.

name: Foundation: rsa-basics
description: n = p*q, ciphertext = m^e mod n; private exponent d. Needed before: rsa-common-modulus, rsa-small-e.

name: Foundation: smart-contract-state
description: How contract state updates across calls and reentrancy risk. Needed before: reentrancy.

name: Foundation: solidity-basics
description: Contracts, msg.sender, storage vs memory, external calls. Needed before: reentrancy.

name: Foundation: stack-layout
description: Local variables, saved frame pointer, return address on the stack. Needed before: format-string, stack-buffer-overflow.

name: Foundation: static-analysis
description: Inspecting binaries/source without running them. Needed before: packed-binary, string-decryption.

name: Foundation: template-engines
description: Server-side templates (Jinja, Twig, etc.) and expression injection. Needed before: ssti.

name: Foundation: web-input-handling
description: How user input reaches sinks (SQL, templates, shells, files). Needed before: path-traversal, sql-injection, ssti, xss-reflected.

name: Foundation: xor-properties
description: XOR is its own inverse; key reuse leaks structure. Needed before: xor-single-byte.
